name: Four Seasons Hotel Philadelphia
positioning: High-rise Four Seasons hotel in Center City Philadelphia with a 57th-floor infinity-edge pool and spa and restaurants by Jean-Georges Vongerichten and Greg Vernick
best_for: Travelers who want skyline views and a Center City base
Guests who want Jean-Georges and Vernick dining on site

facts.text: The hotel is at One North 19th Street, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania 19103.
The hotel is in the heart of Center City at 19th and Arch Streets.
The hotel is a 20 minute drive from Philadelphia International Airport.
Jean-Georges Philadelphia is Chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten's first restaurant in Philadelphia.
Vernick Fish is helmed by James Beard Award-winning Chef Greg Vernick.
The Vernick Fish menu centres on East and West Coast oysters, crudos and seasonal fish.
SkyHigh is a lounge specializing in approachable Jean-Georges cuisine.
The spa has seven treatment rooms.
The hotel's infinity-edge pool is on the 57th floor.
The Fitness Centre is open 24 hours.

highlights.text: The pool is a 30,000-gallon indoor infinity-edge pool overlooking the skyline.
The spa has over 700 lbs. of healing crystals encased into the structure of the walls.
The spa is a Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star Spa.
Dogs are welcomed with plush beds, gourmet treats and a Canine Concierge.
Floral installations by Artistic Director Jeff Leatham can be found in all areas of the hotel.

considerations.text: Condé Nast Traveler describes the Liberty Bell and Independence Park as about a 30-minute walk from the hotel.
The pool area is for registered hotel guests only.
WhataHotel notes the urban setting may lack resort-style outdoor amenities.

perks.text: With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, breakfast for two is free daily.
With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, guests get a priority upgrade if available at check-in.
With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, guests get a $100 hotel credit.
WhataHotel special offers can be combined with the exclusive perks.
With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, guests get free Wi-Fi access.
